title: Chapter 11 – FIDE Online Chess Regulations: Mock Exam

questions.text: What happens to a player's clock if they are disconnected during an online game?

options.text: The clock is paused until the player reconnects
The clock continues to run
The game is immediately declared a draw
The opponent is given extra time

questions.explanation: As per Article E04.11, if a player is disconnected, the clock continues to run. The player must reconnect as quickly as possible. If the disconnection exceeds the specified limit, the arbiter may declare the game lost.

questions.text: Does the touch-move rule apply in online chess?

options.text: Yes, the same as over-the-board play
No, a player may select and deselect a piece until the move is confirmed
Only in supervised online competitions
Only if both players agree before the game

questions.explanation: As per Article E04.3, the touch-move rule does not apply in online play. A player may select and deselect a piece without penalty until the move is confirmed on the platform.

questions.text: In a supervised online competition, what must players keep on at all times?

options.text: Their microphone
Their camera, with face clearly visible
Their screen sharing
Their recording software

questions.explanation: As per Article E04.9, in supervised online competitions, players must keep their camera on at all times and ensure their face is clearly visible. Violations may result in the loss of the game.

questions.text: What is a hybrid chess competition?

options.text: A tournament using both standard and rapid time controls
A competition where some players are physically present and others participate remotely
A competition played on electronic boards in person
A team event combining online and over-the-board players on the same team

questions.explanation: As per Article E04.16, a hybrid chess competition is one in which some players are physically present in the playing venue while others participate remotely. The same Laws of Chess apply to all players.

questions.text: Who has authority to pause, resume, or terminate a game in an online competition?

options.text: The platform's automated system only
Either player by mutual agreement
The arbiter
The tournament organiser

questions.explanation: As per Article E04.10, the arbiter monitors all games and has authority to pause, resume, or terminate a game due to technical issues. The arbiter's decisions are final subject to appeal.

questions.text: What is the virtual clock in online chess?

options.text: A physical clock placed next to the computer
The time display managed by the playing platform's software
A clock shared between both players totalling their combined time
A delay-only timer used for online blitz games

questions.explanation: Per Article E04.4, the virtual clock is the time display managed by the playing platform's software. It functions like a physical digital clock but is controlled entirely by the server hosting the game.

questions.text: Can a player make an illegal move in an officially supervised online game?

options.text: Yes, and the rules for illegal moves are the same as over-the-board
No, the platform software prevents illegal moves from being played
Yes, if the opponent does not notice and claim within 10 seconds
Only in unrated online games

questions.explanation: Per Article E04.5, in online chess the platform software prevents illegal moves from being executed. A player cannot submit an illegal move — it will simply be rejected by the system. Therefore, the Laws on illegal moves do not apply the same way as over-the-board.

questions.text: What is the recommended disconnection threshold before an arbiter may declare a game forfeited in online play?

options.text: 1 minute
5 minutes
Specified by competition rules, but typically between 1–5 minutes
Only if the disconnection is longer than 30 minutes

questions.explanation: Per Article E04.11, the disconnection threshold is specified in the competition regulations. FIDE's guidance is that the arbiter may declare a forfeit only after a prolonged disconnection whose duration is defined in advance — typically between 1 and 5 minutes.

questions.text: What precaution must a player take regarding screen sharing in supervised online play?

options.text: Screen sharing is never required
The player must share their screen with the arbiter if requested
Players must share their screens publicly with all spectators
Screen sharing is only required for World Championships

questions.explanation: Per Article E04.9, in supervised online competitions, the arbiter may require a player to share their screen. The player must comply if asked. This helps the arbiter monitor for anti-cheating compliance.

questions.text: Which FIDE regulation governs online chess competitions?

options.text: A09 — Anti-Cheating Regulations
C04 — Swiss Rules
E04 — Online Chess Regulations
B02 — Rating Regulations

questions.explanation: Per the FIDE Handbook, online chess competitions are governed by regulation E04 — the FIDE Online Chess Regulations. It covers virtual clocks, disconnections, player conduct, supervised play, and hybrid events.
